sentences.text: 1 The Inspector of Police, Mahadevapura Police Station, Bengaluru City, has laid the charge sheet against accused for the offences punishable under Sec. 302,498A, 420 and 328 of IPC.

2. The present case emanates from the first information statement tendered by Sri. Manjunatha D,
S/o Late Devaiah to the Mahadevapura police station on 17.04.2021 at 8.30 p.m and was registered in Cr.No.120/2021.

The gist of prosecution case is that, deceased Smt. Ashwini D and accused were in love with each other and got married with consent of the both families as per the Hindu Customs and rites on 27.05.2018 at Chennambika, Kalyana Mantapa, Holenarasipura Town.

After the marriage, couple lived in a rented house at No.248, 2 nd floor, near Cauvery Water Tank, Narayanapura,
Dooravaninagar, Bangalore.

After some days of marriage, deceased noticed tattooed name of one Roopa on right hand of accused and when deceased questioned, accused told that he had relationship with Roopa and wanted to marry her since deceased had no issues.
3. Even when CW.2 and 3 asked about tattoo, accused abused them and told that he will marry Roopa by killing the deceased.

On 16.04.2021 at 6.00 p.m, both deceased and accused decided to have chicken for dinner along with beer and having a thought of killing his wife, accused searched about poison tablets in Google website and found Disulfiram 250 mg tablets.

Accused visited near by liquor shop by name Swarga Liquors and purchased one Tuborg beer bottle for sum of Rs.145/-
and one plastic glass and went Apollo Pharmacy purchased a strip of Disulfiram tablets 250 Mg by paying Rs.32/-.
Accused came back home at 9.10pm, mixed the said tablets with the beer in a plastic glass without knowledge of deceased and asked her to consume.
She consumed it while having food and fell asleep in her bedroom.

4. At 5.50a.m, accused noticed that deceased was still breathing and alive, with an intention to kill her at about 6.20a.m, strangulated her neck with veil/dupatta and killed her and in order to screen the offense, he misrepresented before CW.5 to 8 by stating that his wife was unconscious and with their help took her to Kaggadasanapura Sri. Lakshmi Hospital in CW.9 Auto and later ran away from the hospital.

After getting information, CW1 and 2 along with relatives came to house of accused, by that time, deceased was shifted to hospital and in hospital they saw the dead body of deceased and noticed compressed marked over the neck and hence CW.1 lodged first information before the SHO.

5. Based on the first information, SHO/CW30 registered FIR no.120/2021 for offences punishable under section sec. 302,109 r/w 34 of IPC, against the accused No.1 to 6 and after completion of investigation, the C.W.30 has filed this charge sheet against accused no. 1 by dropping accused nos.
2 to 6 from the charge sheet for the offences punishable under sections 498A, 302, 420, 328 of IPC .
6. After submitting the charge sheet, learned Magistrate has taken cognizance.

On subsequent date,
the case was committed as the alleged offences are exclusively triable by the Court of Sessions.
After receipt of the records, the Hon'ble Principal City Civil and Sessions Judge, has made over the case to this Court for trial.

2 7.
The Accused has been represented through his counsel.

After hearing both the parties, being satisfied with the prima facie material on record, my predecessor has framed the charges against accused for the offences punishable under sec. 302, 498A, 420 and 328 of IPC.
When read over the same to accused pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried.
Hence, the matter was posted for prosecution evidence.

8. To bring home the guilt of the accused the prosecution got examined in all 13 witnesses as PWs 1 and 13 and produced 26 documents and got marked Ex.P1 to P26 and also identified 10 material object and got marked as MO.1 to MO.10.
After closing the evidence of the prosecution, the statement of accused under section 313 of Cr.P.C., was recorded.
The accused denied all the incriminating circumstances elicited from the prosecution witnesses and he has not chosen to lead any defence evidence on his behalf.
Hence, the matter was posted for arguments on merits.

9. Heard arguments on both sides and perused the records.
10.

On the basis of the materials available on record, the following points arise for my consideration:
1.
Whether the prosecution has proved beyond reasonable doubt that the death of Smt. Ashwini.D, W/o accused is a homicidal?

2. Whether the prosecution has proved beyond reasonable doubts that the accused after marrying the deceased Smt. Ashwini D subjected her to mental and physical harassment and thereby committed an offence punishable under Section 498A of IPC?

3. Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that on 16.04.2021 at 6.00 pm accused and deceased decided to have chicken with Beer for dinner, and accused with intention to kill her purchased a strip of Disulfiram 250 mg tablets in C.W.10 pharmacy and bottle of Tuborg beer and a plastic glass from CW11 Liquor shop to defraud her, he mixed said tablets with beer and made her to drink and become unconscious and thereby he committed an offence punishable under section 420 of Indian Penal Code?

4. Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that on above said date, time and place accused mixed said intoxicating tablets in the beer and made her to drink and become unconscious and thereby he committed an offence punishable under section 328 of Indian Penal Code?

5. Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that on 17.04.2021 at 6.20a.m, when deceased was sleeping in her bedroom, accused noticed that the deceased was still breathing and alive, with intention to cause death, he strangulated her neck with a veil and killed her and thereby committed an offense punishable under Sec.302 of Indian Penal Code?

11. My findings on the above points are as hereunder:
 Point No.1, 2, 4 & 5 : In the  Affirmative  Point No.3 : In the  Negative  Point No.6 : As per final order  for the following:
 :REASONS:
 12. POINT NO.1 : During the course of argument learned Public Prosecutor has submitted that the accused has committed murder of his wife as he was having illicit relationship with another lady by name Roopa and which is evident that name of said lady was tattooed on his right hand and whenever deceased questioned the same, he quarrel with her and said to have told that he will be going to live with said Roopa by killing deceased.
With this motive accused made a plan that on 16.04.2021 in the evening brought a strip of disulfiram tablets from Apollo pharmacy and a bottle of beer with a plastic glass.
With a intention to kill her, he mixed the said tablets with the beer, made her drink with the dinner.
Next day morning he noticed that she was still breathing and alive, he compressed her neck with help of veil and caused the death of deceased.

Further submitted that there are no eye witnesses to the incident and which happened within four walls of the house and only accused resided with deceased and he has to explain what happened to deceased on fateful day.
Further, Ex.P.19 postmortem report very clearly discloses that the death is due to compression of neck and hence death of the deceased is an homicidal in nature.
13. The case of defence is only denial of the prosecution case.
However the counsel for accused made a suggestion to prosecution witness that the deceased was addicted to alcohol and in order to de- addict from alcohol she consumed said tablets.
Accused while recording statement U/sec.313 of Cr.P.C has stated that his wife fainted/unconscious and hence he and others took her to hospital.
It is relevant to note that accused never stated about consumption of de-addiction tablets and moreover he has not explained why and for what reason she was unconscious.

Further on examination of postmortem report which is at Ex.P.19, it reveals that a pressure abrasion seen over the front neck from middle to right side and five superficial contusions seen over the front of neck and which are antemortem in nature and PW.12 who conducted postmortem and opines that death is due to compression of neck.
The Chemical analysis report which is at Ex.P.20, which confirms the presence of traces of Disulfiram.
Even after examining said report, opinion of the PW12 is same as "death is due to compression of neck".
By going through the medical evidence, fact and circumstances of the case, I am of the opinion that the death of deceased is homicidal in nature.
Therefore I answer point no.1 in the affirmative.

When deceased questioned his illicit relationship he started to harassed her physical and mentally, even after advice from the PW1 and PW2 and he said to have told that he will live with said another lady by killing deceased, and with an ulterior motive he purchased intoxicating tablets and mixed with beer and made her to drink and unconscious, and in the next day morning he strangulated her neck with dupatta and committed murder of deceased.
And there is no material to disbelieve the case of prosecution.
